A07-pack-smbus-lead.verdict:
One fact: the P to E pack SMBus lead has no single connector. The two ends belong to different families, have different pitches, pin counts and pin orders, and the assembly document names a third part that matches neither end.

P end: J_SMB is a JST-XH B4B-XH-A, 1x4, 2.50 mm pitch (LCSC C594232, which lcsc_fill.py:158 fills in). Pins: 1 SMBC, 2 SMBD, 3 GND, 4 PRES. The GND on pin 3 is the cell-side ground, upstream of the 2 mohm shunt R10. PRES is pulled low by R14.

E end: J_SMB is a generic 2.54 mm pin header, PinHeader_1x06_P2.54mm_Vertical. It is not JST-PH: the key "PH6" in gen_sch_e.py means pin header. It has no LCSC code; lcsc-allow.txt:7 exempts it as "(XH or pin header)". Pins: 1 SDA0, 2 SCL0, 3 SDA1, 4 SCL1, 5 GND, 6 GND. There is no PRES pin. This pinout is left over from the two SMBus sections of the withdrawn BB-2590/U. Appendix 32.62 kept it by ruling "E6 stays as released".

ASSEMBLY.md:60 says "XH2.5 x 6", with "section A on the kit bus, section B spare". That matches neither board. Section A reaches only E's RP2040, not the kit bus, and section B is E's live sensor bus.

A straight pin-n-to-pin-n lead would do four wrong things:
- It swaps clock and data: P SMBC lands on E SDA0 and P SMBD on E SCL0.
- P's GND lands on SDA1 and holds the sensor bus data line at 0 V. That bus carries the BME688, BMI270, lightning module and pod.
- P's PRES lands on SCL1. It sits at 2.24 V, above the BQ4050's 1.3 V VIH, and every sensor clock pulls it low.
- It carries no ground, because E's GND pins 5 and 6 are left unreached.

Who reads the gauge: only board E's RP2040 U10 can. SDA0 and SCL0 reach nothing but J_SMB, the R34/R35 pull-ups and U10 pins 4 and 5. Those pins are GPIO2 and GPIO3, which on the RP2040 are the I2C1 block, although the net names say 0. The dock carries no I2C. The BQ25731 on A22 is an I2C target at 0x6B on the kit bus (SLUSE66A 9.5.1). It has no conductor to P and no thermistor input. PANEL.md:128 and :155, and appendix 32.62's "the charger BQ25731 of A22 already speaks SMBus to it", are therefore false.

Minimum fix:
1. Make E match P. Change gen_sch_e.py:136 and add an XH4 footprint key. J_SMB becomes a JST-XH 1x4 with 1 SCL0, 2 SDA0, 3 GND, 4 NC. A straight XH-to-XH four-way lead is then correct, and C594232 fills in automatically. Section B loses nothing: its only named use was the withdrawn pack.
2. On P, move J_SMB pin 3 from the cell-side GND to PACK_N, as TI's Figure 21 does. Otherwise the lead's ground wire runs in parallel with the shunt and carries about 5 to 8 percent of the pack current, which the coulomb counter never sees.
3. Correct ASSEMBLY.md:45, :60 and :140, and PANEL.md:128 and :155. Record the correction to 32.62 as a new appendix entry rather than editing it.
4. Add a J_SMB contract to check_contracts.py, which has none today.

Prove each regeneration by a netlist diff (condition 5). This fix does not lift board E's hold (condition 6).

A02-charger-without-host.question: Does the BQ25731 charge without a host (W2: ChargeCurrent 0 A at POR and the 175 s watchdog resets it; W5: 256 mA, refuted by the challenger because SLUSE66A 9.6.2 contradicts itself)? And do W2's F-CH-01 (board A's CELL_BATPRESZ strap is 2S, not 4S) and F-CH-03 (no BATFET, no TS pin) hold?
A02-charger-without-host.verdict:
The BQ25731 itself does charge without a host. It starts at a 256 mA register default, and its watchdog returns ChargeCurrent to 256 mA, not 0 A. TI's applications engineer answered this exact contradiction on E2E thread 1316778 on 23 Jan 2024: "there is a mistake in the description. The POR value is indeed 256mA", and pointed to the BQ25730 for a 0 mA POR. Diffing SLUSE66A against the sibling BQ25730 datasheet (SLUSE65A) confirms it. Every 0 A sentence in SLUSE66A (the 9.6.2 paragraph, the Figure 9-15 caption, 9.6.3 "charge will start when the host writes") is copied word for word from the BQ25730. Every sentence TI edited for the BQ25731 says 256 mA: the 9.6.2 header 0080h, the Table 9-11 bit 7 reset of 1b, 9.3.21.1, the 9.4.1 addition, and Table 9-8's "0 mA 256 mA (BQ25731)". So W2's premise is refuted. W5's 256 mA value is right, but it rests on TI's E2E answer, not on the datasheet alone, so the status is INFERRED with bench confirmation owed.

On board A as designed, however, no charge reaches the pack with or without a host, so W2's conclusion stands on other grounds. F-CH-01 is VERIFIED: R26 60.4k from VDDA and R27 40.2k to ground give 39.96 % (39.48 to 40.44 % at 1 % tolerance), wholly inside the 2S window of 35 to 48.5 %. That matches TI's own 2S example in Figure 10-1. The 2S setting gives ChargeVoltage 8.4 V, SYSOVP 11.7 to 12.2 V (latching, and no register moves it) and BATOVP about 8.6 to 8.8 V. VSYS (pin 22, CH_SRP) sits at the pack voltage through R17, so a 4S pack above about 12 V is never charged. Swapping the two resistors gives 60 %, which selects 3S; W2's 13.3k over 40.2k (75.1 %) is a valid 4S pair.

F-CH-03 is VERIFIED. The part has no battery MOSFET (Features page 1; Device Comparison Table "BATFET Power Path: No") and no thermistor, TS or JEITA input anywhere in the datasheet. On the committed A23 netlist every load hangs on VBAT, behind F1 on the CELL+ side of R17. TI's application puts the system on VSYS instead. The only path from VIN_RAW to VBAT is U2, VBUS20, R16, the charger, R17 and F1. Shore can therefore deliver no more than ChargeCurrent into load and pack together. As designed (2S strap), the kit runs from its pack while shore is connected. Once the strap is fixed and no host is running, shore gives at most 256 mA (3.1 to 4.3 W), below every declared mode's load, so the pack still discharges net.

PANEL.md:155 "a kit with a crashed panel still charges", CONOPS:137 "(by design)" and "HW (charger TS input)", and OPERATING-ENVELOPE.md:89 "the charger's JEITA input" are all false as wired. The one host-free path that does charge is a host that disabled the watchdog (WDTMR_ADJ = 00b) and then crashed: the last ChargeCurrent persists until an adapter removal, a CELL pin going low, or a POR. Side fact missed in round 1: RSNS_RAC defaults to 5 mOhm while board A's R16 is 10 mOhm, so the input-side scaling is wrong until a host fixes it. Band consequences, per held Table 32 (printed pp.58-59; the TOC calls it Table 31) and Table 34 (sensitivity):

(1) Four jacks (ANT0 to ANT3), what the module is designed for:
- DL 4x4 on the Table 2 bands and UL 2x2 on n38/n41/n48/n77/n78/n79.
- Low-band receive diversity.
- LB TX1 for DC_B28_n20 and DC_B20_n28.
- GNSS L1+L5 and LAA.

(2) Two jacks on ANT0+ANT2 (the pairing to use if two):
- Keeps every primary TX0/PRX: LB and MHB on ANT0, UHB and n77/n78/n79 on ANT2.
- Keeps both n77/n78/n79 and n41 transmit paths (TX1/DRX on ANT0), and MHB TX1 for sub-2.6 GHz EN-DC.
- Receive drops to 2 of 4 branches on MHB and UHB, and to primary only on LB. By Table 34, primary against SIMO costs B20 3.9 dB, B28 3.1, B8 2.8, n20 3.7, n28 2.3 and n8 3.0 dB conducted.
- Loses the EN-DC combinations DC_B28_n20 and DC_B20_n28 (footnotes 23/24), LAA, and all of the module's GNSS. The kit's GNSS is the LG290P.

(3) Two jacks on ANT0+ANT1: worse.
- n77/n78/n79 and UHB TX0/PRX sit on ANT2, so the primary transmit and receive path for the main EU 5G band (n78) is not connected.
- Whether the module can run uplink on TX1 alone is not stated (TBD). W4-F10's 'cripples n77/n78' holds only for this pairing.
- LB is as in (2). It keeps GNSS L5 and LAA PRX.

(4) Three jacks on ANT0+ANT2+ANT3:
- Recovers LB diversity, the LB EN-DC combinations, 3 of 4 MHB/UHB branches and GNSS L1.
- Loses only ANT1: PRX MIMO, GNSS L5 and LAA PRX.

- Choosing ANT0+ANT2 over ANT0+ANT1 is engineering: only one option survives Table 32.
- Two, three or four jacks spends money and adds case penetrations. That goes to the owner.

A01-expander-power-up.question: What state do the PCA9555-driven enables on boards A and B (DEV_EN/+5V_DEV via U27, heater, PoE boost, PA/HF software enables, SLOT_EN) take at power-up with the fitted 100k pull-downs, and can the kit boot at all? W2 F-SQ-01 says deadlock; W5 F1 says the internal pull-up makes them come up ON.
A01-expander-power-up.verdict:
Neither claim holds as written. The kit is not deadlocked. It nominally boots as far as the panel controller, but only because of a parameter the datasheet leaves open, not by design. W5 is right about the device rail and wrong about the PoE boost.

1. The fitted part has a pull-up. The expander is the TI PCA9555PWR (LCSC C2864778). Its datasheet (SCPS131J) draws a 100 k resistor from VCC to every I/O pin (Fig 8-2). After power-on reset every pin is an input and the output registers read FFh. The pull-up current IIL has a MAX of -100 uA and no MIN or TYP. The standby "low inputs" current (0.7 mA typ, 1.3 mA max at 3.6 V, 16 inputs) implies about 82 k typical and about 44 k at the strong end. That figure is INFERRED.

2. DEV_EN turns the device rail on nominally.
- The AP64500's EN pin also sources 1 to 2 uA (DS41979). Against R42 (100 k to GND), with A's +3V3 at 3.33 V, DEV_EN sits at 1.71 V (100 k pull-up) to 1.89 V (82 k). The AP64500 turn-on threshold VEN_H is 1.25 V max.
- So +5V_DEV starts, then B's +3V3_DEV, then PANEL_5V, then C's LDO, then the RP2040.
- This fails only if the internal pull-up is weaker than about 181 k: 1.8 times the drawn value, 2.2 times the implied typical. No datasheet limit excludes that. So the result is "nominally ON, not guaranteed", not "deadlock".
- W2 quoted "configured as inputs" but left out section 8.1's pull-up and the AP64500's own EN current.
- It would become a hard deadlock if U27 were swapped for a PCA9535 while R42 stays a pull-down. EN would sit at 0.1 to 0.2 V, below VEN_L min 1.03 V, and there would be no master.

3. Nothing but the panel can write U27. The only master on the kit bus is C's RP2040 on GPIO0/1. It, the bus pull-ups, the STM32 supervisors, the KSZ switch and every B and C device run from +5V_DEV. Board D has only a PCA9555 on the bus. Board E and the CM5s are not on it.

4. Power-up state of each line, until the panel firmware writes the expanders:
- MON_EN, HEAT_EN, D8_EN: 1.66 V nominal against the TPS2596's 1.22 V max turn-on, so asserted. They stay asserted for ever if the panel firmware never runs.
- New finding: U21 (monitor) and U22 (heater) have OVLO dividers of 100 k over 10 k from VBAT. The lockout trips at VBAT 12.87 to 13.42 V. So the monitor and heater conduct only while VBAT is below about 13 V, at power-up and even when commanded. The pack is 14.4 V nominal and 16.8 V full, so the monitor is dark over most of the range.
- POE_EN and PD_EN are OFF. W5 is refuted here. The collapsed LM5176 divider leaves R75 or R134 (10 k) in parallel with the 100 k, so each node sits at 0.30 V nominal and at most 0.74 V at the IIL bound. The LM5176 does not switch below 1.17 V; at the high end it may sit in standby.
- PA_SW_EN and HF_SW_EN: about 1.9 V, inside the LVC08's 0.8 to 2.0 V undefined band.
  - PA_EN and HF_EN are held low while EMCON_HW is low. That is the case while C is unpowered or the ribbon is out (R102).
  - They become undefined once C's +3V3 is up with the EMCON toggle released, which drives EMCON_HW high through U9. That lasts until the firmware writes U27, or for ever if the RP2040 is blank, crashed or in BOOTSEL.
- CHG_INHIBIT: 1.66 V against the 2N7002's 1.0 to 2.5 V threshold, so undefined. Any error is toward the charger being in HiZ.
- B's U6 lines follow the same pattern:
  - LIME_SW_EN, RB_SW_EN, LORA_ON, ZB_ON and CAM_EN are undefined (VIH 2.0 V).
  - KSZ_RST, 5G_OFF and 5G_RESET nominally assert (switch held in reset, 5G off).
  - WL_nDIS, BT_nDIS, RB_IEN and RB_CTRL have no pull-down and go high.
- SLOT_EN1..3 are OFF and guaranteed. A's 100 k pull-downs, plus the RP2040 pad pull-down (50 to 80 k, on at reset) when C is powered, hold them at 0.2 V or less against VEN_L min 1.03 V. They go high only when the panel firmware drives GPIO13 to 15.

5. Boot sequence as wired:
- (S0) Pack connected. The LTC2954 holds RAIL_EN low. All AP64500 and TPS2596 enables are low, since U27 is unpowered.
- (S1) MAIN held for 26 to 41 ms. RAIL_EN is pulled to VBAT by R2, which is over the TPS62933's 6 V EN absolute maximum (F-SQ-02). U12 brings up A's +3V3. KILL is already high through R4 (also over its absolute maximum), and the 400 to 650 ms blanking starts.
- (S2) U27 and U28 come out of reset as inputs with pull-ups. DEV_EN reaches about 1.7 V and U7 soft-starts over 4 ms. Heater and monitor are enabled but gated by OVLO. PoE and PD are off. PA and HF are off because EMCON_HW is low.
- (S3) +5V_DEV brings up D8's 5 V, B's +3V3_DEV and U6, then PANEL_5V, then C's +3V3, the RP2040 and EMCON_HW (high if the toggle is released).
- (S4) The panel firmware must:
  - write the output registers before the configuration registers, keeping DEV_EN=1;
  - keep PI_KILL low;
  - raise SLOT_EN1..3.
  Only then do the CM5s power up. With no panel firmware, the kit stops at S3 with no module running.

6. Minimum fix. These are engineering decisions for the session under the 21 Sep ruling.
- (a) To boot by design, one change: re-terminate R42 from GND to A's +3V3. In gen_sch_a.py, buck5's rpg at :407 needs a per-stage argument, and stage D at :429 passes +3V3.
  - DEV_EN then sits at 3.33 V whenever MAIN has enabled +3V3, whatever the internal pull-up.
  - The panel can still shed the rail by driving the pin low (33 uA).
  - With +3V3 off, EN sits at 0.28 V or less.
- (b) To get defined power-up states without substituting a part, change pull-down values from 100 k to 4.7 k:
  - on A: R21, R103, R104, R111, R112, R113;
  - on B: R48, R50 to R53, optionally R60 to R62.
  The worst case is then 0.49 V or less, below every OFF threshold, at 0.71 mA per line driven high. The alternative, a PCA9535 on U27 and U6, is a part substitution and a mismatch until proven: no datasheet is held and the JLC code is TBD. It must come with (a).
- (c) Firmware contract: output registers before configuration registers. The default output is FFh, so writing configuration first drives POE_EN and PD_EN to 3.3 V and starts both stages. Never write DEV_EN=0 except as the last act of shutdown.
- (d) Resize the U21/U22 OVLO dividers, for example 143 k over 10 k, which trips at 17.9 to 18.7 V.

Not an owner decision.

corrections.correction: F-SQ-01 (lines 181-200, table row 26, JSON findings[1]) is not a VERIFIED deadlock. The fitted TI PCA9555PWR has a 100 k internal pull-up (SCPS131J 8.1, Fig 8-2), and the AP64500 EN pin sources 1 to 2 uA (DS41979). DEV_EN sits at 1.71 V nominal (1.87 V at the ICC-implied 82 k), against VEN_H max 1.25 V. So +5V_DEV and the panel come up nominally. They are not guaranteed to: IIL has no minimum, and the rail fails only above about 181 k. Keep it critical as 'no designed power-up path: the device rail depends on an unspecified expander parameter'. Keep the fix. Add that a PCA9535 on U27 without re-terminating R42 makes it a real deadlock. Item 4 (slots enabled only by the panel) stands.

F-SQ-04 (lines 221-228): 'name the internal node distinctly' restores 62 k over 10 k from a 3.33 V logic line. That puts 0.46 V on EN/UVLO, below VEN(OP) min 1.17 V, so the PA, HF, PoE and PD stages would never run. The fix must re-size or drop the divider, for example keep the logic line direct and use a separate VBAT UVLO. Note also that the collapsed divider's 10 k (R75, R134) is what holds POE_EN and PD_EN off at power-up. Re-check that when the divider changes.

New finding, VERIFIED, for the power workstream. U21 (monitor, VMON) and U22 (heater, VHEAT) are TPS259631 eFuses with OVLO dividers of 100 k 1% over 10 k 1% from VBAT (gen_sch_a.py:526-528; A23 netlist U21_OVLO and U22_OVLO). Against VOVLO(R) of 1.17 to 1.22 V (SLVSET8A 7.5 and 8.3.2.1), they lock out at VBAT 12.87 to 13.42 V and recover below 11.9 to 12.4 V. VBAT is declared 14.4 V nominal and 16.8 V at work (gen_sch_a.py:28). So the Xenarc monitor and the heater mat are off over most of the pack range, whatever MON_EN and HEAT_EN say. Fix: resize, for example 143 k over 10 k, which trips at 17.9 to 18.7 V, below the TPS2596's 19 V recommended maximum. Minor: U23's OVLO pin sits at 0.46 V, below the 0.5 V recommended range.

F1 (lines 70-90) and row S1 (line 61) need four changes.
(1) Remove the PoE boost from the ON list, and PD_EN too. POE_EN and PD_EN have R75 or R134 (10 k to GND) in parallel with the 100 k (A23 netlist). Each node is at 0.30 V nominal and at most 0.74 V at the IIL bound. The LM5176 VEN(OP) min is 1.17 V, so neither stage switches.
(2) PA_SW_EN, HF_SW_EN and CHG_INHIBIT are UNDEFINED at about 1.9 V and 1.66 V, not 'above the enable thresholds'. The error on CHG_INHIBIT is toward the charger being in HiZ.
(3) Heater and monitor enables are asserted nominally, but the eFuses conduct only while VBAT is below about 13 V (OVLO, see the W2 correction).
(4) The voltage claim is INFERRED nominal, not VERIFIED. The PCA9535 swap is a part substitution, a mismatch until proven: no datasheet is held and the JLC code is TBD. It must be paired with the R42 re-termination, otherwise it creates a hard deadlock.
Firmware contract in section 6: write the output registers (default FFh) before the configuration registers. Writing configuration first drives POE_EN and PD_EN to 3.3 V and starts both stages. Never write DEV_EN=0 except as the last act of shutdown, because it removes the panel's own supply and U27 holds that state until +3V3 falls.
